items.stem: Across the test region of a high-impedance electrometer bench, charges −14 nC and +3 nC are mounted 0.6 m apart along a horizontal line, with −14 nC on the left. An axial sensor at exterior point P sits 0.9 m to the right of −14 nC. Use k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² for free-space electrostatic interactions. What is the resultant electric field at exterior point P?
items.workedSolution: Exterior point P is r₁ = 0.9 m to the right of −14 nC and r₂ = 0.9 − 0.6 = 0.3 m to the right of +3 nC. Superposing E_x = kq₁/r₁² + kq₂/r₂² gives 144 N C⁻¹ to the right (A).

markScheme.criterion: Uses r₁ = 0.9 m and r₂ = 0.3 m to obtain 144 N C⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: Within an evacuated spacecraft charge-control test cell, isolated point charges +9 nC at x = 0 and +16 nC at x = 0.7 m are mounted along a straight insulating track. How far from the +9 nC point charge does the net electric field vanish?
items.workedSolution: Equating opposing field magnitudes gives q₁/x² = q₂/(0.7 − x)², so (0.7 − x)/x = √(16/9). Solving yields x = 0.7 × √9/(√9 + √16) = 0.300 m (B).

markScheme.criterion: Equates kq₁/x² = kq₂/(0.7 − x)² to obtain x = 0.300 m (B).

items.stem: Inside a university physics Van de Graaff calibration tunnel, stationary point charges +7 nC (left) and −4 nC (right) are mounted 0.6 m apart, with axial point P located 0.3 m from the left charge. A small probe charge of +4 nC is placed at P without disturbing the fixed sources. Model the region as vacuum with Coulomb constant k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the resultant electrostatic force acting on the +4 nC probe charge?
items.workedSolution: At P (r₁ = 0.3 m, r₂ = 0.3 m), the resultant electric field is E = 1.10 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right. Multiplying by q_test = +4 nC gives F = q_test E = 4.40 × 10⁻⁶ N to the right (A).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates E = 1.10 × 10³ N C⁻¹ and F = qE = 4.40 × 10⁻⁶ N to the right (A).

items.stem: During a central elastic nuclear encounter in vacuum, an incident alpha particle carrying charge +2e reaches a minimum centre-to-centre separation of 3.2 × 10⁻¹⁴ m from a heavy iron nucleus of charge +26e. Take k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻², e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, and zero electric potential at infinity. What is the electrostatic potential energy of the system at closest approach, expressed in electronvolts (eV)?
items.workedSolution: At r_min, V = kZe / r_min = 1.17 × 10⁶ V. For a +2e projectile, E_p = 2eV = 2.34 × 10⁶ eV (D).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates V = 1.17 × 10⁶ V and E_p = 2V (in eV) = 2.34 × 10⁶ eV (D).

items.stem: Within a shielded Faraday enclosure used for sensor testing, stationary charges +6 nC (on the left) and +24 nC (on the right) sit at separation 0.6 m. With zero potential set at infinity in vacuum, use k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the electric potential at the unique point on the line between the charges where the resultant electric field is zero?
items.workedSolution: Zero field occurs at x = 0.6 × √6/(√6 + √24) = 0.200 m from +6 nC (and 0.400 m from +24 nC). Scalar potentials add: V = k(q₁/x + q₂/(d − x)) = 809 V (A).

markScheme.criterion: Finds x = 0.200 m and sums positive scalar potentials to obtain 809 V (A).

items.stem: A droplet of oil (density 860 kg m⁻³) falls at 9.00 × 10⁻⁵ m s⁻¹ in air ($\eta = 1.80 \times 10^{-5}\text{ Pa s}$, $g = 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$) and is held stationary by 592 V across plates 10.0 mm apart.
items.workedSolution: (a) $W = 2.84 × 10⁻¹⁴ N$. (b) $Q = 4.79 × 10⁻¹⁹ C$. (c) all measured droplet charges are integer multiples of the elementary charge proving charge is quantised.

markScheme.criterion: Calculates $r = 9.30 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}$ using Stokes law.
Evaluates $W = 6\pi\eta r v$ or $\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \rho g$.
Correct weight 2.84 × 10⁻¹⁴ N.
Applies $Q = Wd / V$.
Correct charge 4.79 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
States every measured charge is an integer multiple of $1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$.
Concludes electric charge is quantised in discrete units of $e$.

parts.prompt: Calculate the weight of the oil droplet.
Calculate the charge $Q$ on the droplet.
Explain how repeating this calculation for many droplets led to the concept of charge quantisation.
parts.expectedAnswer: Millikan found that all measured droplet charges are integer multiples of the elementary charge proving charge is quantised, never smaller fractions of $1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$.
workingSteps: Every measured droplet charge was a whole-number multiple of $1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$.
Hence charge exists in discrete packets of the elementary charge $e$.

items.stem: In a dry-nitrogen micro-electrostatics apparatus, fixed charges +5Q (left) and +18Q (right) sit along an axis in free space separated by 4 x. Point P is marked 1 x to the right of +5Q. Write the resultant electric field magnitude at P in the form E = α kQ/x², where k is the Coulomb constant.
items.workedSolution: (a) The left positive charge produces a larger repulsive field magnitude at P than the right positive charge, so the net electric field points to the right. (b) α = |5/1² − 18/3²| = |5.00 − 2.00| = 3.00.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant direction as to the right with valid reasoning.
Forms inverse-square terms 5/1² and 18/3².
Subtracts the opposing dimensionless field coefficients.
Obtains α = 3.00.

items.stem: Inside a university physics Van de Graaff calibration tunnel, a point charge q₁ = 9 × 10⁻⁹ C sits at x = 0 and an unknown point charge q₂ sits at x = 0.6 m. An axial field scan locates a zero-field null point between them at x = 0.36 m.
items.workedSolution: (a) q₁ and q₂ have the same sign so their fields oppose between them. (b) |q₂/q₁| = ((0.6 − 0.36)/0.36)² = (0.24/0.36)² = 0.444. (c) q₂ = +(0.444)(9 × 10⁻⁹ C) = +4.00 × 10⁻⁹ C.

markScheme.criterion: States same sign because fields must oppose in the region between the charges.
Uses |q₂/q₁| = ((d − x₀)/x₀)² with d − x₀ = 0.24 m.
Obtains 0.444.
Multiplies q₁ by ratio from (b) with positive sign.
Obtains q₂ = +4.00 × 10⁻⁹ C.

parts.prompt: State whether q₁ and q₂ have the same sign or opposite signs, explaining your reasoning.
parts.expectedAnswer: They have the same sign because their individual electric field vectors must point in opposite directions to cancel between the charges.
workingSteps: Opposite-sign charges produce fields in the same direction everywhere between them.
Therefore q₁ and q₂ must have the same sign.

parts.prompt: Calculate the ratio |q₂ / q₁|.
workingSteps: Distance from q₂ to null point = 0.6 − 0.36 = 0.24 m.

parts.prompt: Hence determine the signed value of q₂.
workingSteps: q₂ is positive (same sign as q₁) with magnitude 0.444 × 9 × 10⁻⁹ C.

items.stem: Inside an electrostatic ink-droplet test nozzle in vacuum, across a 0.06 m vacuum gap with potential difference 2400 V, a singly charged argon ion carrying +1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 6.63 × 10⁻²⁶ kg accelerates from rest from the positive plate to the 0 V plate. Ignore gravitational and relativistic effects.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E = V / d.
Obtains 4.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹.
Equates kinetic energy gain to electrical work qV.
Obtains 3.84 × 10⁻¹⁶ J.
Rearranges ½mv² = ΔE_k for v = √(2ΔE_k / m).

Determine the kinetic energy gained by the singly charged argon ion on reaching the 0 V plate.
Hence calculate the speed of the singly charged argon ion as it reaches the 0 V plate.

items.stem: Along a horizontal ceramic support rod in free space, collinear charges +6 nC (left) and +2 nC (right) are held at a separation of 0.4 m, while point P is marked 0.15 m from the +6 nC charge. Take the Coulomb constant as k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². Which option states the net electric field vector at P?
items.workedSolution: Between like-sign charges, the individual fields at P oppose each other: |E₁| = k|q₁|/(0.15)² = 2.40 × 10³ N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/(0.25)² = 288 N C⁻¹. Subtracting gives |E_net| = 2.11 × 10³ N C⁻¹ directed to the right (D).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field contributions to obtain 2.11 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (D).

items.stem: Along the symmetry line of a miniature ion-optics bench, two opposite-sign sources of −9 nC on the left and +3 nC on the right have separation 0.8 m; axial point P is situated 0.6 m from −9 nC. Assume vacuum (k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²) and reference all scalar potentials to zero at infinity. Although the electric potential at P is zero, what is the resultant electric field at P?
items.workedSolution: Even though V = kq₁/r₁ + kq₂/r₂ = 0 at P, the potential gradient dV/dx is non-zero because both opposite charges drive a positive test charge to the left: E = 225 N C⁻¹ + 674 N C⁻¹ = 899 N C⁻¹ to the left (C).

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes E != 0 when V = 0 and sums collinear contributions to obtain 899 N C⁻¹ to the left (C).

items.stem: Between parallel titanium electrodes inside a beam-diagnostics chamber, two parallel conducting plates separated by 0.04 m are maintained at a potential difference of 320 V (from 320 V on the left plate to 0 V on the right plate). A positively charged droplet of charge +8 × 10⁻⁹ C and mass 4 × 10⁻⁶ kg is released at the 320 V plate. Ignore edge effects. What is the magnitude of the uniform electric field between the plates?
items.workedSolution: For uniform parallel plates, E = V / d = 320 / 0.04 = 8.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: In a microfluidic electrophoresis test cell (modelled in vacuum), three planar equipotentials are established labelled 300 V, 180 V, and 60 V from left to right at uniform spacing 0.04 m. Released from rest on the 180 V middle equipotential, a charged dielectric bead (m = 1.5 × 10⁻⁵ kg, q = +2.5 × 10⁻⁸ C) accelerates horizontally across one spacing to the 60 V line. What is the magnitude of the horizontal electrostatic acceleration of the charged dielectric bead?

markScheme.criterion: Finds E = 3.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹ and a = qE/m = 5.00 m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: Across the test region of a high-impedance electrometer bench, two stationary charges of −6 nC on the left and −9 nC on the right have separation 0.5 m, with point P marked 0.2 m from the left source. Use 1/(4πε₀) = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² with the reference of zero potential at infinite separation.
items.workedSolution: (a) Scalar potential V = k(q₁/0.2 + q₂/0.3) = −539 V. (b) Vector electric field E = 449 N C⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: Applies signed scalar sum V = k(q₁/r₁ + q₂/r₂).
Obtains V = −539 V (including sign if negative).
Uses inverse-square magnitudes at r₁ = 0.2 m and r₂ = 0.3 m.
Combines the two collinear field vectors with proper directions.
Obtains 449 N C⁻¹ to the left.

items.stem: An empty air-filled parallel-plate capacitor (area 500 cm², separation 0.500 mm, ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹) is charged through a 22 kΩ resistor from a constant 60.0 V supply. How much thermal energy (in nanojoules) is dissipated in the circuit resistance during complete charging?
items.workedSolution: C₀ = ε₀A/d = 885 pF. Half of battery work QV is dissipated as heat: E_heat = ½C₀V² = 1.59e+3 nJ.

markScheme.criterion: Applies 50% charging loss E_heat = ½C₀V² = 1.59e+3 nJ.

items.stem: Across the test region of a high-impedance electrometer bench, charges +4 nC and −12 nC are separated horizontally by 0.8 m, with +4 nC on the left. Observation point P is situated between them, 0.3 m from the left-hand source. Adopt the free-space constant k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². Which row gives the magnitude and direction of the electric field vector at P?
items.workedSolution: At P, both opposite-sign sources drive a positive test charge to the right. |E₁| = k|q₁|/r₁² = 400 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/r₂² = 432 N C⁻¹ (with r₂ = 0.5 m). Summing the two same-sense vectors gives E = 831 N C⁻¹ to the right (A).

markScheme.criterion: Adds same-direction inverse-square contributions to obtain 831 N C⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: Within a dust-plasma levitation chamber evacuated to low pressure, along a 0.5 m axis between +8 nC on the left and −3 nC on the right, a +3.2 nC probe particle rests momentarily at point P (0.2 m from +8 nC). Model the charges in free space (k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²), taking V = 0 at infinity.
items.workedSolution: (a) E = 2.10 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right. (b) Scalar sum V = k(q₁/0.2 + q₂/0.3) = 270 V. (c) Force on probe F = q_test E = 6.71 × 10⁻⁶ N to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Applies vector superposition E_x = kq₁/r₁² + kq₂/r₂².
Obtains 2.10 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right.
Sums signed scalar potentials k(q₁/r₁ + q₂/r₂).
Obtains 270 V.
Uses F = q_test E with correct sign/direction.
Obtains 6.71 × 10⁻⁶ N to the right.

items.stem: Along the optical axis of a benchtop ion-trap demonstration rig, fixed charges +7Q (left) and +8Q (right) sit along an axis in free space separated by 3 x. Point P is marked 1 x to the right of +7Q. Using Coulomb constant k, what is the resultant electric field at P expressed in terms of kQ/x²?
items.workedSolution: At P, +7Q produces (7/1²) kQ/x² = 7.00 kQ/x² to the right, while +8Q at distance 2 x produces (8/2²) kQ/x² = 2.00 kQ/x² to the left. Net field = 5.00 kQ/x² to the right (B).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts (7/1²) and (8/2²) to obtain 5.00 kQ/x² to the right (B).

items.stem: Inside an electrostatic aerosol-charging test section, two fixed point charges q₁ and q₂ are separated by 0.9 m in vacuum, with q₁ = 5 × 10⁻⁹ C on the left. Measurements along the connecting axis show that the resultant electric field is zero at a distance of 0.3 m from q₁. What is the signed charge q₂?
items.workedSolution: An interior null point requires q₁ and q₂ to have the same sign (+). Equating kq₁/x₀² = kq₂/(d − x₀)² with d − x₀ = 0.6 m gives q₂ = q₁((0.6)/(0.3))² = 4.00 × 5 × 10⁻⁹ C = +2.00 × 10⁻⁸ C (C).

markScheme.criterion: Uses q₂ = q₁((d − x₀)/x₀)² with positive sign to obtain +2.00 × 10⁻⁸ C (C).

items.stem: Across the uniform-field region of a parallel-plate guard-ring cell, a singly charged lithium ion (charge +1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 1.16 × 10⁻²⁶ kg) starts from rest at a planar electrode at +900 V and accelerates in vacuum across a 0.03 m gap to a parallel grounded electrode at 0 V. Neglecting gravity, what speed does the singly charged lithium ion reach upon arriving at the 0 V plate?
items.workedSolution: By conservation of energy, ½mv² = qV, so v = √(2qV / m) = √(2 × 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ × 900 / 1.16 × 10⁻²⁶) = 1.58 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ (D).

markScheme.criterion: Equates ½mv² = qV to obtain v = 1.58 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Within a laboratory quadrupole pre-alignment vacuum housing, fixed point charges −9 nC (at x = 0) and −2 nC (at x = 0.5 m) occupy a straight insulating rail. Point P is situated at x = 0.2 m. Use k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² for free-space electrostatic interactions.
items.workedSolution: (a) Both negative sources attract a positive test charge placed at P, so the left charge pulls leftward while the right charge pulls rightward. (b) |E₁| = k|q₁|/(0.2)² = 2.02 × 10³ N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/(0.3)² = 200 N C⁻¹. Subtracting the opposing vectors yields 1.82 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: States that a positive test charge between like-sign sources experiences opposite forces from the left and right charges.
Evaluates E = k|q|/r² at r₁ = 0.2 m and r₂ = 0.3 m.
Subtracts the two opposing field magnitudes.
Obtains 1.82 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left.

items.stem: Across the test region of a high-impedance electrometer bench, two opposite-sign sources of +6 nC on the left and −18 nC on the right have separation 0.8 m; axial point P is situated 0.2 m from +6 nC. Take k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and define electric potential to be zero at infinity.
items.workedSolution: (a) V = k(6 × 10⁻⁹/0.2 + -18 × 10⁻⁹/0.6) = 0 V. (b) At P both fields point to the right, giving E = 1.35 × 10³ N C⁻¹ + 450 N C⁻¹ = 1.80 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right.

Obtains V = 0 V.
Applies inverse-square law E = k|q|/r² to both sources.
Adds the two collinear field magnitudes.

Calculate the magnitude and state the direction of the resultant electric field at point P.

items.stem: Across the parallel accelerating gap of a semiconductor ion implanter, flat parallel plates spaced 0.04 m apart establish a 600 V potential drop as a micro-carrier (mass 3 × 10⁻⁶ kg, charge +1.5 × 10⁻⁸ C) moves from the positive plate to the earthed 0 V plate. Neglect edge effects and gravitational forces.
items.workedSolution: (a) Uniform field E = V / d = 600 / 0.04 = 1.50 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. (b) Work done by the field W = qV = (1.5 × 10⁻⁸)(600) = 9.00 × 10⁻⁶ J.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes V = 600 V and d = 0.04 m into E = V / d.
Obtains 1.50 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹.
Applies W = qV (or W = qEd).
Obtains 9.00 × 10⁻⁶ J.

items.stem: Within an electrostatic lens drift space, three parallel vertical equipotential planes are observed labelled 420 V, 240 V, and 60 V from left to right at uniform spacing 0.06 m. Released from rest on the 240 V middle equipotential, a charged dielectric bead (m = 3 × 10⁻⁵ kg, q = +5 × 10⁻⁸ C) accelerates horizontally across one spacing to the 60 V line.
items.workedSolution: (a) E = (240 − 60) / 0.06 = 3.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹ to the right. (b) a = qE / m = 5.00 m s⁻². (c) Using ½mv² = q(180), v = 0.775 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides adjacent potential step by spacing s.
Obtains 3.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹ to the right.
Applies a = qE / m.
Obtains 5.00 m s⁻².
Equates ½mv² = q(180) or uses v² = 2as.
Obtains 0.775 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Across the measurement track of a non-contact Kelvin probe bench, two stationary charges of −9 nC on the left and +5 nC on the right have separation 0.6 m, with point P marked 0.2 m from the left source. Use 1/(4πε₀) = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² with the reference of zero potential at infinite separation. What is the electric potential at point P?
items.workedSolution: Electric potential is a signed scalar: V = k(q₁/r₁ + q₂/r₂) with r₁ = 0.2 m and r₂ = 0.4 m. Thus V = −405 V + (112 V) = −292 V (A).

markScheme.criterion: Sums signed scalar potentials kq₁/0.2 + kq₂/0.4 = −292 V (A).

items.stem: A parallel-plate capacitor (area 250 cm², gap 0.500 mm, ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹) stays connected to a 20.0 V supply while a dielectric slab (εᵣ = 5.00) is slid fully between its plates. Calculate the final energy stored in nanojoules.
items.workedSolution: C' = ε₀εᵣA/d = 2.21e+3 pF. At constant V = 20.0 V, E' = ½C'V² = 443 nJ.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates stored energy 443 nJ.

items.stem: Along the symmetry line of a miniature ion-optics bench, an axial probe point P sits 0.4 m from a left-hand −4.5 nC point charge along the 0.9 m segment connecting it to a right-hand +9 nC point charge. Treat both sources as point charges in vacuum with k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Both individual electric field vectors at P point to the left (toward the negative left source and away from the positive right source), so they reinforce toward the left. (b) With r₁ = 0.4 m and r₂ = 0.5 m, |E₁| = 253 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = 324 N C⁻¹. Summing gives 576 N C⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: Explains using a positive test charge that both source fields at P act in the same direction.
Applies E = k|q|/r² with r₁ = 0.4 m and r₂ = 0.5 m.
Adds the two collinear field magnitudes.
Obtains 576 N C⁻¹ to the left.

workingSteps: |E₁| = k|q₁|/r₁² = 253 N C⁻¹; |E₂| = k|q₂|/r₂² = 324 N C⁻¹.

items.stem: In a dry-nitrogen micro-electrostatics apparatus, point sources +12 nC at x = 0 and −5 nC at x = 0.8 m remain fixed while a small probe of charge −2 nC is placed at x = 0.3 m (point P). Take k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and define electric potential to be zero at infinity. What is the electric potential at P due to the two fixed source charges?
items.workedSolution: Electric potential at P depends only on the source charges: V = k(q₁/0.3 + q₂/0.5) = 360 V + (−89.9 V) = 270 V (A).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates V = k(q₁/0.3 + q₂/0.5) = 270 V (A), independent of q_test.

items.stem: Along the central axis of a precision Coulomb torsion module, a point charge +18 nC is fixed at x = 0 and a second point charge −5 nC is fixed at x = 0.6 m. Exterior point P lies further to the right along the positive x-axis at x = 1 m (so P is 0.4 m to the right of −5 nC). Use 1/(4πε₀) = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² throughout. What is the resultant electric field at exterior point P?
items.workedSolution: Exterior point P is r₁ = 1 m to the right of +18 nC and r₂ = 1 − 0.6 = 0.4 m to the right of −5 nC. Superposing E_x = kq₁/r₁² + kq₂/r₂² gives 119 N C⁻¹ to the left (C).

markScheme.criterion: Uses r₁ = 1 m and r₂ = 0.4 m to obtain 119 N C⁻¹ to the left (C).

items.stem: Along the central axis of a precision Coulomb torsion module, along a 0.6 m baseline in free space, a +1 nC point charge is fixed at the left end and a +4 nC point charge is fixed at the right end. Determine the distance x from the left-hand +1 nC source to the zero-field null point between the charges.
items.workedSolution: Equating opposing field magnitudes gives q₁/x² = q₂/(0.6 − x)², so (0.6 − x)/x = √(4/1). Solving yields x = 0.6 × √1/(√1 + √4) = 0.200 m (A).

markScheme.criterion: Equates kq₁/x² = kq₂/(0.6 − x)² to obtain x = 0.200 m (A).

items.stem: On an insulated fused-quartz metrology rail in vacuum, along a 0.75 m baseline, isolated charges +3 nC and +12 nC are fixed at the left and right ends respectively. Adopt k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and zero electrostatic potential at infinite distance. What is the electric potential at the unique point on the line between the charges where the resultant electric field is zero?

markScheme.criterion: Finds x = 0.250 m and sums positive scalar potentials to obtain 324 V (D).

items.stem: Robert Millikan's oil-drop experiment provided the first direct precision measurement of the elementary charge $e$ and combined with Thomson's $e/m$ yielded the mass of the electron.
items.workedSolution: Level 3 synthesis: terminal velocity with field off yields droplet radius via Stokes law and balancing the stationary droplet with electric field reveals quantised charge; covers apparatus, Stage 1 Stokes radius derivation, explicit physical assumptions, Stage 2 $QV/d = mg$, and charge quantisation.

markScheme.criterion: Describes experimental arrangement (sprayed oil droplets between parallel plates separation $d$, illuminated and timed via calibrated microscope).
Explains Stage 1 (field off): measuring constant terminal velocity $v$ and equating $6\pi\eta r v = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \rho g$ to deduce $r$ and $m$.
States explicit physical assumptions: spherical droplet, laminar airflow, and negligible upthrust from air.
Explains Stage 2 (field on): adjusting $V$ to hold the droplet stationary and applying $QV/d = mg$ to compute $Q$.
Explains quantisation conclusion: all measured charges and ionisation steps are integer multiples of $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$.
Notes combining Millikan's $e$ with Thomson's $e/m$ determined the electron rest mass $m_e$.

parts.prompt: Describe the experimental procedure, measurements, physical assumptions, and equations used in Millikan's oil-drop experiment to determine a droplet's charge, and explain the significance of repeating the measurement across many droplets.
parts.expectedAnswer: Millikan's experiment uses a two-stage force balance in which terminal velocity with field off yields droplet radius via Stokes law and balancing the stationary droplet with electric field reveals quantised charge. Fine oil droplets sprayed from an atomiser become charged by friction and enter a chamber between horizontal parallel plates of measured separation $d$, illuminated from the side and viewed through a travelling microscope with a calibrated graticule. In Stage 1 (electric field off), a droplet falls at constant terminal velocity $v$ (measured by timing its passage across graticule divisions). Assuming the droplet is spherical, moves slowly in laminar airflow, and air upthrust is negligible, viscous Stokes drag balances weight: $6\pi\eta r v = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \rho g$, which yields droplet radius $r = \sqrt{9\eta v / (2\rho g)}$ and hence mass $m = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \rho$. In Stage 2 (electric field on), the plate potential difference $V$ is adjusted until the droplet hovers completely stationary, where upward electrostatic force equals weight: $QV/d = mg$, giving $Q = mgd/V$. Repeating this across hundreds of droplets revealed that every measured charge—and every step change after X-ray ionisation—was an integer multiple of $1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$, proving that electric charge is quantised and enabling calculation of electron mass $m_e$ from Thomson's $e/m$.
workingSteps: Describe apparatus: atomiser, parallel plates separation $d$, variable DC supply $V$, illumination, and calibrated microscope.
Stage 1 (field off): time constant terminal fall speed $v$ across known vertical distance.
Apply Stokes' law $6\pi\eta r v = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \rho g$ to derive radius $r$ and mass $m$.
State key assumptions: spherical droplet, slow laminar flow, negligible air upthrust.
Stage 2 (field on): adjust $V$ to hold droplet stationary so $QV/d = mg$ gives $Q = mgd/V$.
Explain significance: all charges are integer multiples of $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$ (charge quantisation) and determine $m_e$ via Thomson's $e/m$.

items.stem: On a sapphire isolation substrate inside a cleanroom vacuum stage, on a straight vacuum baseline of total length 3 x between +7Q on the left and +4Q on the right, point P lies 2 x from the left source. Write the resultant electric field magnitude at P in the form E = α kQ/x², where k is the Coulomb constant.
items.workedSolution: (a) The right positive charge produces a larger repulsive field magnitude at P than the left positive charge, so the net electric field points to the left. (b) α = |7/2² − 4/1²| = |1.75 − 4.00| = 2.25.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant direction as to the left with valid reasoning.
Forms inverse-square terms 7/2² and 4/1².
Subtracts the opposing dimensionless field coefficients.
Obtains α = 2.25.

parts.prompt: Calculate the numerical value of the dimensionless coefficient α.
workingSteps: Leftward term from +4Q at distance 1 x: 4/1² = 4.00.

items.stem: Along a horizontal ceramic support rod in free space, fixed sources q₁ (left, 2 × 10⁻⁹ C) and q₂ (right) lie 1 m apart. The electric field vanishes at an interior point 0.2 m to the right of q₁.
items.workedSolution: (a) q₁ and q₂ have the same sign so their fields oppose between them. (b) |q₂/q₁| = ((1 − 0.2)/0.2)² = (0.8/0.2)² = 16.0. (c) q₂ = +(16.0)(2 × 10⁻⁹ C) = +3.20 × 10⁻⁸ C.

markScheme.criterion: States same sign because fields must oppose in the region between the charges.
Uses |q₂/q₁| = ((d − x₀)/x₀)² with d − x₀ = 0.8 m.
Obtains 16.0.
Multiplies q₁ by ratio from (b) with positive sign.
Obtains q₂ = +3.20 × 10⁻⁸ C.

parts.prompt: State whether q₁ and q₂ have the same sign or opposite signs, explaining your reasoning.
parts.expectedAnswer: They have the same sign because their individual electric field vectors must point in opposite directions to cancel between the charges.
workingSteps: Opposite-sign charges produce fields in the same direction everywhere between them.
Therefore q₁ and q₂ must have the same sign.

parts.prompt: Calculate the ratio |q₂ / q₁|.
workingSteps: Distance from q₂ to null point = 1 − 0.2 = 0.8 m.

parts.prompt: Hence determine the signed value of q₂.
workingSteps: q₂ is positive (same sign as q₁) with magnitude 16.0 × 2 × 10⁻⁹ C.

items.stem: Between two planar molybdenum grids of an ion-thruster prototype, a deuteron (charge +1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 3.34 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) starts from rest at a planar electrode at +800 V and accelerates in vacuum across a 0.05 m gap to a parallel grounded electrode at 0 V. Ignore gravitational and relativistic effects.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E = V / d.
Obtains 1.60 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹.
Equates kinetic energy gain to electrical work qV.
Obtains 1.28 × 10⁻¹⁶ J.
Rearranges ½mv² = ΔE_k for v = √(2ΔE_k / m).
Obtains 2.77 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹.

Determine the kinetic energy gained by the deuteron on reaching the 0 V plate.
Hence calculate the speed of the deuteron as it reaches the 0 V plate.

items.stem: Along the reference baseline of an electrostatic beam-steering rig, a left-hand source of +3 nC and a right-hand source of +12 nC are separated by 0.5 m. An axial test point P is located 0.3 m to the right of +3 nC. Use k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² for free-space electrostatic interactions. What is the resultant electric field at point P?
items.workedSolution: Between like-sign charges, the individual fields at P oppose each other: |E₁| = k|q₁|/(0.3)² = 300 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/(0.2)² = 2.70 × 10³ N C⁻¹. Subtracting gives |E_net| = 2.40 × 10³ N C⁻¹ directed to the left (B).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field contributions to obtain 2.40 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left (B).

items.stem: Along the reference baseline of an electrostatic beam-steering rig, opposite point charges +4 nC (left) and −4 nC (right) are fixed 0.4 m apart. Point P lies on the connecting axis 0.2 m from +4 nC, where the scalar electric potential vanishes. Assume vacuum (k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²) and reference all scalar potentials to zero at infinity. Although the electric potential at P is zero, what is the resultant electric field at P?
items.workedSolution: Even though V = kq₁/r₁ + kq₂/r₂ = 0 at P, the potential gradient dV/dx is non-zero because both opposite charges drive a positive test charge to the right: E = 899 N C⁻¹ + 899 N C⁻¹ = 1.80 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (A).

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes E != 0 when V = 0 and sums collinear contributions to obtain 1.80 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: In an evacuated parallel-plate velocity-calibration gap, a potential difference of 1600 V is applied across parallel planar electrodes spaced 0.08 m apart. A test micro-sphere carrying charge +1.5 × 10⁻⁸ C and mass 3 × 10⁻⁶ kg crosses from the positive electrode to the grounded 0 V electrode. Determine the electrical work performed by the uniform field during the full transit to the 0 V electrode.
items.workedSolution: Electrical work done across the full potential difference is W = qΔV = (1.5 × 10⁻⁸)(1600) = 2.40 × 10⁻⁵ J (D).

items.stem: In a dry-nitrogen micro-electrostatics apparatus, point charges +4 nC (left) and −12 nC (right) are fixed 0.8 m apart, and point P lies on the line between them 0.5 m from +4 nC. Take k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and define electric potential to be zero at infinity.
items.workedSolution: (a) Scalar potential V = k(q₁/0.5 + q₂/0.3) = −288 V. (b) Vector electric field E = 1.34 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right.

Uses inverse-square magnitudes at r₁ = 0.5 m and r₂ = 0.3 m.
Combines the two collinear field vectors with proper directions.
Obtains 1.34 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right.

items.stem: A slab of polar dielectric material is slid smoothly to fill the air gap between the charged plates of a parallel-plate capacitor. How do the polar molecules increase the capacitance?
items.workedSolution: In the applied field, polar molecules rotate to align negative ends toward the positive plate, producing an opposing internal electric field that reduces net field and increases capacitance by relative permittivity. Therefore the correct statement is: The polar molecules rotate to align negative ends toward the positive plate, producing an opposing internal electric field that reduces net field and increases capacitance by relative permittivity

options.text: The polar molecules conduct free electrons directly across the gap to equalise plate potentials.
options.distractorRationale: A dielectric is an insulator; conduction across the gap would discharge the capacitor.

options.label: B
options.text: The polar molecules rotate to align negative ends toward the positive plate, producing an opposing internal electric field that reduces net field and increases capacitance by relative permittivity

options.label: C
options.text: The polar molecules align positive ends toward the positive plate, reinforcing the applied field and raising potential difference.
options.distractorRationale: Reverses dipole orientation and electric field direction.

options.label: D
options.text: The polar molecules physically push the metal plates further apart so capacitance increases with separation.
options.distractorRationale: Increasing separation d decreases capacitance since C = ε₀εᵣA/d.

items.stem: In a dry-nitrogen micro-electrostatics apparatus, two fixed point charges of −8 nC (left) and +5 nC (right) are held 0.7 m apart. Point P lies on the straight line joining them at a distance of 0.3 m to the right of the −8 nC charge. Assume vacuum permittivity such that k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². items.stem: In a Geiger–Marsden alpha-scattering recoil analysis, an incident alpha particle carrying charge +2e reaches a minimum centre-to-centre separation of 3.8 × 10⁻¹⁴ m from a heavy gold nucleus of charge +79e. Take k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻², e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, and zero electric potential at infinity.
items.workedSolution: (a) V = kZe / r_min = 2.99 × 10⁶ V. (b) E_p = 2eV = 9.57 × 10⁻¹³ J. (c) Dividing by e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J eV⁻¹ gives 5.98 × 10⁶ eV.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes Q = 79e and r_min = 3.8 × 10⁻¹⁴ m into V = kQ/r.
Obtains 2.99 × 10⁶ V.
Multiplies potential from (a) by projectile charge 2e.
Obtains 9.57 × 10⁻¹³ J.
Divides joule energy by 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J eV⁻¹ (or multiplies V in volts by z).
Obtains 5.98 × 10⁶ eV.

parts.prompt: Calculate the electric potential due to the gold nucleus at distance r_min.
Calculate the electrostatic potential energy (in joules) of the alpha particle at closest approach.
Express this electrostatic potential energy in electronvolts (eV).
workingSteps: E_p (in eV) = E_p (in J) / (1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J eV⁻¹) = 5.98 × 10⁶ eV.

items.stem: Within a dust-plasma levitation chamber evacuated to low pressure, along a 0.85 m baseline, isolated charges +32 nC and +2 nC are fixed at the left and right ends respectively. Adopt k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and zero electrostatic potential at infinite distance.
items.workedSolution: (a) Setting 32/x² = 2/(0.85 − x)² gives x = 0.680 m. (b) Scalar potentials add: V = k(q₁/x + q₂/(d − x)) = 529 V. (c) By definition of the null point (zero potential gradient), E = 0 N C⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Equates 32/x² = 2/(0.85 − x)².
Obtains x = 0.680 m.
Adds positive scalar potential contributions kq₁/x + kq₂/(d − x).
Obtains V = 529 V.
States 0 N C⁻¹.

Calculate the electric potential at point X.
State the magnitude of the resultant electric field at X even though the potential there is non-zero.

items.stem: A charged oil droplet of weight $2.84 \times 10^{-14}\text{ N}$ is held motionless between parallel plates 10.0 mm apart by a potential difference of 592 V. Given $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$, how many excess elementary charges are on the droplet?
items.workedSolution: $Q = \frac{Wd}{V} = \frac{2.84 \times 10^{-14} \times 0.0100}{592} = 4.80 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$. Dividing by $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$ gives $n = 3.0$ excess electrons.

markScheme.criterion: Correct calculated value 3.0.

items.stem: On an insulated fused-quartz metrology rail in vacuum, on a straight vacuum baseline of total length 3 x between +9Q on the left and +2Q on the right, point P lies 2 x from the left source. Using Coulomb constant k, what is the resultant electric field at P expressed in terms of kQ/x²?
items.workedSolution: At P, +9Q produces (9/2²) kQ/x² = 2.25 kQ/x² to the right, while +2Q at distance 1 x produces (2/1²) kQ/x² = 2.00 kQ/x² to the left. Net field = 0.250 kQ/x² to the right (C).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts (9/2²) and (2/1²) to obtain 0.250 kQ/x² to the right (C).

items.stem: Across the measurement track of a non-contact Kelvin probe bench, along a 0.8 m vacuum baseline with q₁ = 3 × 10⁻⁹ C at the left end and q₂ at the right end, the net electric field is zero at a point 0.2 m from q₁. What is the magnitude ratio |q₂ / q₁|?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ((d − x₀)/x₀)² = (0.6/0.2)² = 9.00 (B).

items.stem: Inside a vacuum micro-machined capacitive sensor gap, parallel extraction plates separated by 0.06 m are held at 1200 V and 0 V. A stationary alpha particle of mass 6.64 × 10⁻²⁷ kg and charge +3.2 × 10⁻¹⁹ C is released from the 1200 V plate. Neglecting gravity, what speed does the alpha particle reach upon arriving at the 0 V plate?
items.workedSolution: By conservation of energy, ½mv² = qV, so v = √(2qV / m) = √(2 × 3.2 × 10⁻¹⁹ × 1200 / 6.64 × 10⁻²⁷) = 3.40 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ (C).

markScheme.criterion: Equates ½mv² = qV to obtain v = 3.40 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Across the test region of a high-impedance electrometer bench, collinear charges +8 nC (left) and +2 nC (right) are held at a separation of 0.5 m, while point P is marked 0.2 m from the +8 nC charge. Take the Coulomb constant as k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Both positive sources repel a positive test charge placed at P, so the left charge pushes rightward while the right charge pushes leftward. (b) |E₁| = k|q₁|/(0.2)² = 1.80 × 10³ N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/(0.3)² = 200 N C⁻¹. Subtracting the opposing vectors yields 1.60 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: States that a positive test charge between like-sign sources experiences opposite forces from the left and right charges.
Evaluates E = k|q|/r² at r₁ = 0.2 m and r₂ = 0.3 m.
Subtracts the two opposing field magnitudes.
Obtains 1.60 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right.

items.stem: Within an evacuated spacecraft charge-control test cell, fixed charges −7 nC at x = 0 and +7 nC at x = 0.7 m establish a zero-potential point P on the axis at x = 0.35 m. Model the charges in free space (k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²), taking V = 0 at infinity.
items.workedSolution: (a) V = k(-7 × 10⁻⁹/0.35 + 7 × 10⁻⁹/0.35) = 0 V. (b) At P both fields point to the left, giving E = 514 N C⁻¹ + 514 N C⁻¹ = 1.03 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes signed charges with r₁ = 0.35 m and r₂ = 0.35 m into V = k(q₁/r₁ + q₂/r₂).
Obtains V = 0 V.
Applies inverse-square law E = k|q|/r² to both sources.
Adds the two collinear field magnitudes.
Obtains 1.03 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left.

items.stem: Inside a high-voltage electrostatic precipitator test cell, two parallel conducting plates separated by 0.04 m are maintained at a potential difference of 2000 V (from 2000 V on the left plate to 0 V on the right plate). A positively charged droplet of charge +8 × 10⁻⁹ C and mass 4 × 10⁻⁶ kg is released at the 2000 V plate. Neglect edge effects and gravitational forces.
items.workedSolution: (a) Uniform field E = V / d = 2000 / 0.04 = 5.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. (b) Work done by the field W = qV = (8 × 10⁻⁹)(2000) = 1.60 × 10⁻⁵ J.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes V = 2000 V and d = 0.04 m into E = V / d.
Obtains 5.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹.
Applies W = qV (or W = qEd).
Obtains 1.60 × 10⁻⁵ J.

items.stem: Inside a parallel-grid ion-retarding analyzer, three adjacent equipotential surfaces are charted labelled 260 V, 150 V, and 40 V from left to right at uniform spacing 0.055 m. Released from rest on the 150 V middle equipotential, a charged dielectric bead (m = 2.2 × 10⁻⁵ kg, q = +4 × 10⁻⁸ C) accelerates horizontally across one spacing to the 40 V line.
items.workedSolution: (a) E = (150 − 40) / 0.055 = 2.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹ to the right. (b) a = qE / m = 3.64 m s⁻². (c) Using ½mv² = q(110), v = 0.632 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides adjacent potential step by spacing s.
Obtains 2.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹ to the right.
Applies a = qE / m.
Obtains 3.64 m s⁻².
Equates ½mv² = q(110) or uses v² = 2as.
Obtains 0.632 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Along a horizontal ceramic support rod in free space, point charges −4 nC (left) and −8 nC (right) are fixed 0.6 m apart, and point P lies on the line between them 0.2 m from −4 nC. Assume vacuum (k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²) and reference all scalar potentials to zero at infinity. What is the electric potential at point P?
items.workedSolution: Electric potential is a signed scalar: V = k(q₁/r₁ + q₂/r₂) with r₁ = 0.2 m and r₂ = 0.4 m. Thus V = −180 V + (−180 V) = −360 V (D).

markScheme.criterion: Sums signed scalar potentials kq₁/0.2 + kq₂/0.4 = −360 V (D).

items.stem: An air-filled parallel-plate capacitor is charged to voltage V and then disconnected from the battery so it is electrically isolated. A polar dielectric slab of relative permittivity εᵣ is then inserted between the plates. What happens to its voltage and stored energy?
items.workedSolution: For an isolated capacitor, charge stays constant so potential difference and stored energy decrease by factor relative permittivity. Therefore the correct statement is: Because it is isolated, charge stays constant so potential difference and stored energy decrease by factor relative permittivity

markScheme.criterion: Selects correct conceptual explanation: charge stays constant so potential difference and stored energy decrease by factor relative permittivity.

options.distractorRationale: Violates conservation of charge on isolated plates.

items.stem: Along the primary axis of a precision field-mill calibration bench, two fixed point charges of +2.5 nC (left) and −5 nC (right) are held 0.5 m apart. Point P lies on the straight line joining them at a distance of 0.2 m to the right of the +2.5 nC charge. Adopt the free-space constant k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Both individual electric field vectors at P point to the right (away from the positive left source and toward the negative right source), so they reinforce toward the right. (b) With r₁ = 0.2 m and r₂ = 0.3 m, |E₁| = 562 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = 499 N C⁻¹. Summing gives 1.06 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Explains using a positive test charge that both source fields at P act in the same direction.
Applies E = k|q|/r² with r₁ = 0.2 m and r₂ = 0.3 m.
Adds the two collinear field magnitudes.
Obtains 1.06 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right.

parts.prompt: State and explain why the two individual electric field contributions reinforce rather than oppose each other at point P.
parts.expectedAnswer: Both individual electric field vectors at P point to the right (away from the positive left source and toward the negative right source), so they reinforce toward the right.
workingSteps: Electric field direction is the force direction on a positive test charge.
Both individual electric field vectors at P point to the right (away from the positive left source and toward the negative right source), so they reinforce toward the right.

parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude and state the direction of the resultant electric field at point P.
workingSteps: |E₁| = k|q₁|/r₁² = 562 N C⁻¹; |E₂| = k|q₂|/r₂² = 499 N C⁻¹.
Resultant E = |E₁| + |E₂| = 1.06 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right.

items.stem: Inside a university physics Van de Graaff calibration tunnel, along a 0.7 m axis between +11 nC on the left and −4 nC on the right, a −2.2 nC probe particle rests momentarily at point P (0.3 m from +11 nC). Use 1/(4πε₀) = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² with the reference of zero potential at infinite separation. What is the electric potential at P due to the two fixed source charges?
items.workedSolution: Electric potential at P depends only on the source charges: V = k(q₁/0.3 + q₂/0.4) = 330 V + (−89.9 V) = 240 V (D).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates V = k(q₁/0.3 + q₂/0.4) = 240 V (D), independent of q_test.

items.stem: Along the symmetry line of a miniature ion-optics bench, two collinear point charges of −12 nC (left) and +5 nC (right) are separated by 0.4 m. Point P lies outside the pair to the right of both charges, at a total distance of 0.7 m from the left-hand −12 nC charge. Adopt the free-space constant k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the resultant electric field at exterior point P?
items.workedSolution: Exterior point P is r₁ = 0.7 m to the right of −12 nC and r₂ = 0.7 − 0.4 = 0.3 m to the right of +5 nC. Superposing E_x = kq₁/r₁² + kq₂/r₂² gives 279 N C⁻¹ to the right (D).

markScheme.criterion: Uses r₁ = 0.7 m and r₂ = 0.3 m to obtain 279 N C⁻¹ to the right (D).

items.stem: Along a horizontal ceramic support rod in free space, isolated point charges +4 nC at x = 0 and +16 nC at x = 0.9 m are mounted along a straight insulating track. At what distance from the +4 nC charge along the line joining the charges is the resultant electric field equal to zero?
items.workedSolution: Equating opposing field magnitudes gives q₁/x² = q₂/(0.9 − x)², so (0.9 − x)/x = √(16/4). Solving yields x = 0.9 × √4/(√4 + √16) = 0.300 m (B).

markScheme.criterion: Equates kq₁/x² = kq₂/(0.9 − x)² to obtain x = 0.300 m (B).

items.stem: Along a straight dielectric mounting rod inside an evacuated bell jar, stationary point charges +6 nC (left) and −3 nC (right) are mounted 0.5 m apart, with axial point P located 0.2 m from the left charge. A small probe charge of −4 nC is placed at P without disturbing the fixed sources. Adopt the free-space constant k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the resultant electrostatic force acting on the −4 nC probe charge?
items.workedSolution: At P (r₁ = 0.2 m, r₂ = 0.3 m), the resultant electric field is E = 1.65 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right. Multiplying by q_test = −4 nC gives F = q_test E = 6.59 × 10⁻⁶ N to the left (A).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates E = 1.65 × 10³ N C⁻¹ and F = qE = 6.59 × 10⁻⁶ N to the left (A).

Obtains W_field = −1.80 × 10⁻⁶ J (with correct sign).

items.stem: During a nuclear physics beamline scattering run, a projectile alpha particle of charge +2e approaches head-on a stationary bismuth nucleus of atomic number Z = 83 (charge +83e) to a distance of closest approach r_min = 5.2 × 10⁻¹⁴ m. Take k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻², e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, and zero electric potential at infinity. What is the electric potential due to the bismuth nucleus at distance r_min?
items.workedSolution: Radial potential of the +83e nucleus is V = kZe / r_min = (8.99 × 10⁹ × 83 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹) / (5.2 × 10⁻¹⁴) = 2.30 × 10⁶ V (A).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates V = kZe / r_min = 2.30 × 10⁶ V (A).

items.stem: In a dry-nitrogen micro-electrostatics apparatus, two fixed positive point charges of +1 nC (left) and +25 nC (right) are held 0.6 m apart. Use 1/(4πε₀) = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² with the reference of zero potential at infinite separation. What is the electric potential at the unique point on the line between the charges where the resultant electric field is zero?
items.workedSolution: Zero field occurs at x = 0.6 × √1/(√1 + √25) = 0.100 m from +1 nC (and 0.500 m from +25 nC). Scalar potentials add: V = k(q₁/x + q₂/(d − x)) = 539 V (C).

markScheme.criterion: Finds x = 0.100 m and sums positive scalar potentials to obtain 539 V (C).

items.stem: Along the central axis of a precision Coulomb torsion module, two isolated positive sources of charge +10Q and +4Q have separation 3 x, with +10Q at the left end. Observation point P is positioned between them at distance 2 x from +10Q. Write the resultant electric field magnitude at P in the form E = α kQ/x², where k is the Coulomb constant.
items.workedSolution: (a) The right positive charge produces a larger repulsive field magnitude at P than the left positive charge, so the net electric field points to the left. (b) α = |10/2² − 4/1²| = |2.50 − 4.00| = 1.50.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant direction as to the left with valid reasoning.
Forms inverse-square terms 10/2² and 4/1².
Subtracts the opposing dimensionless field coefficients.
Obtains α = 1.50.

items.stem: Across the test region of a high-impedance electrometer bench, along a 0.8 m vacuum baseline with q₁ = 2.5 × 10⁻⁸ C at the left end and q₂ at the right end, the net electric field is zero at a point 0.5 m from q₁.
items.workedSolution: (a) q₁ and q₂ have the same sign so their fields oppose between them. (b) |q₂/q₁| = ((0.8 − 0.5)/0.5)² = (0.3/0.5)² = 0.360. (c) q₂ = +(0.360)(2.5 × 10⁻⁸ C) = +9.00 × 10⁻⁹ C.

markScheme.criterion: States same sign because fields must oppose in the region between the charges.
Uses |q₂/q₁| = ((d − x₀)/x₀)² with d − x₀ = 0.3 m.
Obtains 0.360.
Multiplies q₁ by ratio from (b) with positive sign.
Obtains q₂ = +9.00 × 10⁻⁹ C.

Model the charges in free space (k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²), taking V = 0 at infinity. Although the electric potential at P is zero, what is the resultant electric field at P?
items.workedSolution: Even though V = kq₁/r₁ + kq₂/r₂ = 0 at P, the potential gradient dV/dx is non-zero because both opposite charges drive a positive test charge to the right: E = 599 N C⁻¹ + 300 N C⁻¹ = 899 N C⁻¹ to the right (D).

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes E != 0 when V = 0 and sums collinear contributions to obtain 899 N C⁻¹ to the right (D).

items.stem: Between precision-spaced invar plates in a metrology vacuum tank, inside an evacuated cell of gap width 0.032 m biased at 640 V, a charged aerosol particle of mass 7 × 10⁻⁶ kg and charge +3.5 × 10⁻⁸ C travels from the +640 V electrode to the 0 V collector. Neglecting fringing at the plate edges, calculate the uniform electric field strength in the gap.
items.workedSolution: For uniform parallel plates, E = V / d = 640 / 0.032 = 2.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Within an evacuated deflection cell, three parallel equipotential planes are maintained at 280 V (left), 160 V (middle), and 40 V (right), with adjacent lines spaced 0.03 m apart. A charged dielectric bead of mass 2.7 × 10⁻⁵ kg and charge +4.5 × 10⁻⁸ C starts from rest on the middle 160 V line and moves frictionlessly horizontally to the 40 V line. What is the magnitude and direction of the uniform electric field?
items.workedSolution: Electric field points toward decreasing potential (to the right) with magnitude E = |ΔV|/s = (160 − 40) / 0.03 = 4.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹ to the right (B).

markScheme.criterion: Uses E = −ΔV/Δx to obtain 4.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹ to the right (B).

items.stem: Along the central axis of a precision Coulomb torsion module, point charges −10 nC (left) and +4 nC (right) are fixed 0.7 m apart, and point P lies on the line between them 0.3 m from −10 nC. Take k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and define electric potential to be zero at infinity.
items.workedSolution: (a) Scalar potential V = k(q₁/0.3 + q₂/0.4) = −210 V. (b) Vector electric field E = 1.22 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: Applies signed scalar sum V = k(q₁/r₁ + q₂/r₂).
Obtains V = −210 V (including sign if negative).
Uses inverse-square magnitudes at r₁ = 0.3 m and r₂ = 0.4 m.
Combines the two collinear field vectors with proper directions.
Obtains 1.22 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left.

Calculate the magnitude and state the direction of the resultant electric field at point P.
workingSteps: Use vector superposition E_x = kq₁/r₁² + kq₂/r₂² (right positive).
Resultant E = 1.22 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left.

items.stem: An air-spaced parallel-plate capacitor is charged to 27.0 V and isolated from the power supply. A polar dielectric slab of relative permittivity 3.60 is then inserted to fill the gap. Calculate the new potential difference across the plates.
items.workedSolution: Isolated Q is fixed and C' = εᵣC, so V' = Q / C' = V₀ / εᵣ = 27.0 / 3.60 = 7.50 V.

markScheme.criterion: Computes V' = V₀ / εᵣ = 7.50 V.

items.stem: Along a straight dielectric mounting rod inside an evacuated bell jar, fixed sources carrying +2 nC (on the left) and −9 nC (on the right) have a centre-to-centre separation of 0.5 m. Point P is marked 0.2 m from the +2 nC source along the connecting line. Model the region as vacuum with Coulomb constant k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the resultant electric field strength and direction at P?
items.workedSolution: At P, both opposite-sign sources drive a positive test charge to the right. |E₁| = k|q₁|/r₁² = 449 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/r₂² = 899 N C⁻¹ (with r₂ = 0.3 m). Summing the two same-sense vectors gives E = 1.35 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (D).

markScheme.criterion: Adds same-direction inverse-square contributions to obtain 1.35 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (D).

items.stem: Within a shielded Faraday enclosure used for sensor testing, along a 0.6 m axis between +6 nC on the left and +9 nC on the right, a −1.5 nC probe particle rests momentarily at point P (0.2 m from +6 nC). Use 1/(4πε₀) = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² with the reference of zero potential at infinite separation.
items.workedSolution: (a) E = 843 N C⁻¹ to the right. (b) Scalar sum V = k(q₁/0.2 + q₂/0.4) = 472 V. (c) Force on probe F = q_test E = 1.26 × 10⁻⁶ N to the left.

markScheme.criterion: Applies vector superposition E_x = kq₁/r₁² + kq₂/r₂².
Obtains 843 N C⁻¹ to the right.
Sums signed scalar potentials k(q₁/r₁ + q₂/r₂).
Obtains 472 V.
Uses F = q_test E with correct sign/direction.
Obtains 1.26 × 10⁻⁶ N to the left.

items.stem: Within an evacuated spacecraft charge-control test cell, fixed sources +12 nC (left) and −3 nC (right) have separation 0.3 m. Observation point P is positioned on the extended axis beyond the right-hand charge, 0.5 m from +12 nC. Treat both sources as point charges in vacuum with k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Because P lies to the right of both opposite-sign charges, one source repels a positive test charge rightward while the other attracts it leftward, so their fields oppose. (b) Using r₁ = 0.5 m and r₂ = 0.2 m, |E₁| = 432 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = 674 N C⁻¹, giving resultant E = 243 N C⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: States opposite directions with correct test-charge reasoning.
Identifies r₁ = 0.5 m and r₂ = 0.2 m.
Applies signed vector superposition kq₁/r₁² + kq₂/r₂².
Obtains 243 N C⁻¹ to the left.

items.stem: On an insulated fused-quartz metrology rail in vacuum, isolated point charges +4 nC at x = 0 and +25 nC at x = 0.7 m are mounted along a straight insulating track.
items.workedSolution: (a) Between two positive charges their repulsive fields act in opposite directions, and equal field magnitudes require a smaller distance from the weaker left-hand charge. (b) Setting 4/x² = 25/(0.7 − x)² gives (0.7 − x)/x = √(25/4), hence x = 0.200 m.

markScheme.criterion: Explains opposing fields between positive sources and identifies closer proximity to the left-hand charge.
Equates inverse-square field magnitudes 4/x² = 25/(0.7 − x)².
Takes square roots correctly to linearize for x.
Obtains x = 0.200 m.

items.stem: Across a heavy-ion electrostatic stopping-distance calculation, a stationary lead target nucleus (charge +82e) repels an incoming triply charged lithium nucleus (charge +3e) that momentarily comes to rest at separation 6.4 × 10⁻¹⁴ m. items.workedSolution: (a) V = kZe / r_min = 1.84 × 10⁶ V. (b) E_p = 3eV = 8.85 × 10⁻¹³ J. (c) Dividing by e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J eV⁻¹ gives 5.53 × 10⁶ eV.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes Q = 82e and r_min = 6.4 × 10⁻¹⁴ m into V = kQ/r.

Obtains 8.85 × 10⁻¹³ J.
Divides joule energy by 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J eV⁻¹ (or multiplies V in volts by z).
Obtains 5.53 × 10⁶ eV.

Adds positive scalar potential contributions kq₁/x + kq₂/(d − x).
Obtains V = 216 V.
States 0 N C⁻¹.

items.stem: Along the primary axis of a precision field-mill calibration bench, positive point charges +4Q (on the left) and +18Q (on the right) are fixed a distance 4 x apart in vacuum. Point P lies on the line joining them at a distance 1 x from +4Q (and 3 x from +18Q). Using Coulomb constant k, what is the resultant electric field at P expressed in terms of kQ/x²?
items.workedSolution: At P, +4Q produces (4/1²) kQ/x² = 4.00 kQ/x² to the right, while +18Q at distance 3 x produces (18/3²) kQ/x² = 2.00 kQ/x² to the left. Net field = 2.00 kQ/x² to the right (D).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts (4/1²) and (18/3²) to obtain 2.00 kQ/x² to the right (D).

items.stem: Along the symmetry line of a miniature ion-optics bench, a point charge q₁ = 8 × 10⁻⁹ C sits at x = 0 and an unknown point charge q₂ sits at x = 0.5 m. An axial field scan locates a zero-field null point between them at x = 0.2 m. What is the magnitude ratio |q₂ / q₁|?
items.workedSolution: At x₀ = 0.2 m, the distance from q₂ is d − x₀ = 0.3 m. Setting |q₁|/x₀² = |q₂|/(d − x₀)² gives |q₂/q₁| = (0.3/0.2)² = 2.25 (D).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ((d − x₀)/x₀)² = (0.3/0.2)² = 2.25 (D).

items.stem: Inside an electrostatic dust-accelerator launch stage, parallel extraction plates separated by 0.04 m are held at 600 V and 0 V. A stationary charged polymer droplet of mass 1.2 × 10⁻⁹ kg and charge +4 × 10⁻¹² C is released from the 600 V plate. Neglecting gravity, what speed does the charged polymer droplet reach upon arriving at the 0 V plate?
items.workedSolution: By conservation of energy, ½mv² = qV, so v = √(2qV / m) = √(2 × 4 × 10⁻¹² × 600 / 1.2 × 10⁻⁹) = 2.00 m s⁻¹ (B).

markScheme.criterion: Equates ½mv² = qV to obtain v = 2.00 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: On a sapphire isolation substrate inside a cleanroom vacuum stage, along a 0.6 m baseline between fixed charges +9 nC on the left and +3 nC on the right, point P lies 0.2 m from the left source. Model the region as vacuum with Coulomb constant k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². Determine the resultant electric field strength and sense at P.
items.workedSolution: Between like-sign charges, the individual fields at P oppose each other: |E₁| = k|q₁|/(0.2)² = 2.02 × 10³ N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/(0.4)² = 169 N C⁻¹. Subtracting gives |E_net| = 1.85 × 10³ N C⁻¹ directed to the right (A).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field contributions to obtain 1.85 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: Within a dust-plasma levitation chamber evacuated to low pressure, along the 0.8 m line segment between −2 nC (left) and +6 nC (right), point P sits 0.2 m from the left source. With zero potential set at infinity in vacuum, use k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². Although the electric potential at P is zero, what is the resultant electric field at P?
items.workedSolution: Even though V = kq₁/r₁ + kq₂/r₂ = 0 at P, the potential gradient dV/dx is non-zero because both opposite charges drive a positive test charge to the left: E = 449 N C⁻¹ + 150 N C⁻¹ = 599 N C⁻¹ to the left (D).

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes E != 0 when V = 0 and sums collinear contributions to obtain 599 N C⁻¹ to the left (D).

items.stem: Across a parallel-plate electron-beam calibration diode, planar parallel plates at potentials 1200 V and 0 V have separation 0.06 m in vacuum, accelerating a charged bead of mass 2.5 × 10⁻⁶ kg and charge +1.25 × 10⁻⁸ C across the full gap. What uniform electric field magnitude acts across the space between the parallel electrodes?
items.workedSolution: For uniform parallel plates, E = V / d = 1200 / 0.06 = 2.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Across the central region of a wide guard-ring capacitor, three vertical equipotential lines are drawn with potentials 150 V, 90 V, and 30 V from left to right separated by 0.02 m between neighbouring lines. A charged dielectric bead carrying +3.2 × 10⁻⁸ C and mass 1.6 × 10⁻⁵ kg is released at rest on the 90 V line along a horizontal frictionless axis. What speed does the charged dielectric bead reach at the 30 V equipotential line?

items.stem: Inside an ultra-high-vacuum electrostatic calibration chamber, point charges +15 nC (left) and −6 nC (right) are fixed 0.9 m apart, and point P lies on the line between them 0.5 m from +15 nC. Adopt k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and zero electrostatic potential at infinite distance. What is the electric potential at point P?
items.workedSolution: Electric potential is a signed scalar: V = k(q₁/r₁ + q₂/r₂) with r₁ = 0.5 m and r₂ = 0.4 m. Thus V = 270 V + (−135 V) = 135 V (C).

markScheme.criterion: Sums signed scalar potentials kq₁/0.5 + kq₂/0.4 = 135 V (C).

items.stem: A student replaces the charging resistor in an RC circuit with another resistor of four times the resistance and recharges the same capacitor from empty using the same ideal battery. How does the total thermal energy dissipated in the resistor change?
items.workedSolution: Regardless of R, the battery supplies energy Q V while the capacitor stores half Q V so exactly fifty percent is dissipated as thermal energy in circuit resistance regardless of resistance value. Therefore the correct statement is: It is unchanged because the battery supplies energy Q V while the capacitor stores half Q V so exactly fifty percent is dissipated as thermal energy in circuit resistance regardless of resistance value

markScheme.criterion: Selects correct conceptual explanation: battery supplies energy Q V while the capacitor stores half Q V so exactly fifty percent is dissipated as thermal energy in circuit resistance regardless of resistance value.

items.stem: Within an evacuated spacecraft charge-control test cell, fixed sources carrying −5 nC (on the left) and +10 nC (on the right) have a centre-to-centre separation of 0.6 m. Point P is marked 0.2 m from the −5 nC source along the connecting line. Take the Coulomb constant as k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². Determine the magnitude and direction of the net electric field at point P.
items.workedSolution: At P, both opposite-sign sources drive a positive test charge to the left. |E₁| = k|q₁|/r₁² = 1.12 × 10³ N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/r₂² = 562 N C⁻¹ (with r₂ = 0.4 m). Summing the two same-sense vectors gives E = 1.69 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left (D).

markScheme.criterion: Adds same-direction inverse-square contributions to obtain 1.69 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left (D).

items.stem: Along the central axis of a precision Coulomb torsion module, along a 0.7 m axis between +4 nC on the left and +10 nC on the right, a −2.4 nC probe particle rests momentarily at point P (0.3 m from +4 nC). Model the charges in free space (k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²), taking V = 0 at infinity. What is the electric potential at P due to the two fixed source charges?
items.workedSolution: Electric potential at P depends only on the source charges: V = k(q₁/0.3 + q₂/0.4) = 120 V + (225 V) = 345 V (D).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates V = k(q₁/0.3 + q₂/0.4) = 345 V (D), independent of q_test.

items.stem: Within an evacuated spacecraft charge-control test cell, two collinear point charges of +12 nC (left) and −3 nC (right) are separated by 0.3 m. Point P lies outside the pair to the right of both charges, at a total distance of 0.5 m from the left-hand +12 nC charge. Treat both sources as point charges in vacuum with k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the resultant electric field at exterior point P?
items.workedSolution: Exterior point P is r₁ = 0.5 m to the right of +12 nC and r₂ = 0.5 − 0.3 = 0.2 m to the right of −3 nC. Superposing E_x = kq₁/r₁² + kq₂/r₂² gives 243 N C⁻¹ to the left (D).

markScheme.criterion: Uses r₁ = 0.5 m and r₂ = 0.2 m to obtain 243 N C⁻¹ to the left (D).

items.stem: Inside a university physics Van de Graaff calibration tunnel, along a 0.8 m baseline in free space, a +1 nC point charge is fixed at the left end and a +9 nC point charge is fixed at the right end. How far from the +1 nC point charge does the net electric field vanish?
items.workedSolution: Equating opposing field magnitudes gives q₁/x² = q₂/(0.8 − x)², so (0.8 − x)/x = √(9/1). Solving yields x = 0.8 × √1/(√1 + √9) = 0.200 m (A).

markScheme.criterion: Equates kq₁/x² = kq₂/(0.8 − x)² to obtain x = 0.200 m (A).

items.stem: Across the test region of a high-impedance electrometer bench, source charges +8 nC at x = 0 and +2 nC at x = 0.5 m are held stationary, while point P sits on the axis at x = 0.2 m. A small probe charge of −2 nC is placed at P without disturbing the fixed sources. Take the Coulomb constant as k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the resultant electrostatic force acting on the −2 nC probe charge?
items.workedSolution: At P (r₁ = 0.2 m, r₂ = 0.3 m), the resultant electric field is E = 1.60 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right. Multiplying by q_test = −2 nC gives F = q_test E = 3.20 × 10⁻⁶ N to the left (C).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates E = 1.60 × 10³ N C⁻¹ and F = qE = 3.20 × 10⁻⁶ N to the left (C).

items.stem: Inside a uniform-field drift chamber, three equally spaced planar equipotential lines are recorded at 360 V (left), 200 V (middle), and 40 V (right), with adjacent lines separated by 0.05 m. A particle of charge −1.25 × 10⁻⁸ C moves from the 360 V line to the 40 V line. What signed work does the electric field do on the charge?
items.workedSolution: Work done by the electric field is W_field = q(V_initial − V_final) = (−1.25 × 10⁻⁸ C)(360 − (40)) = −4.00 × 10⁻⁶ J (A).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W_field = q(V_i − V_f) = −4.00 × 10⁻⁶ J (A).

items.stem: Modelling a head-on nuclear collision below the fusion threshold, an incident alpha particle carrying charge +2e reaches a minimum centre-to-centre separation of 6 × 10⁻¹⁴ m from a heavy uranium nucleus of charge +92e. Take k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻², e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, and zero electric potential at infinity. What is the electric potential due to the uranium nucleus at distance r_min?
items.workedSolution: Radial potential of the +92e nucleus is V = kZe / r_min = (8.99 × 10⁹ × 92 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹) / (6 × 10⁻¹⁴) = 2.21 × 10⁶ V (B).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates V = kZe / r_min = 2.21 × 10⁶ V (B).

items.stem: Within a laboratory quadrupole pre-alignment vacuum housing, two fixed positive point charges of +3 nC (left) and +27 nC (right) are held 0.9 m apart. With zero potential set at infinity in vacuum, use k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the electric potential at the unique point on the line between the charges where the resultant electric field is zero?
items.workedSolution: Zero field occurs at x = 0.9 × √3/(√3 + √27) = 0.225 m from +3 nC (and 0.675 m from +27 nC). Scalar potentials add: V = k(q₁/x + q₂/(d − x)) = 479 V (C).

markScheme.criterion: Finds x = 0.225 m and sums positive scalar potentials to obtain 479 V (C).

items.stem: An oil droplet of mass $8.05 \times 10^{-15}\text{ kg}$ carrying a net charge of $9.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$ is held completely stationary between horizontal parallel plates. Taking $g = 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$, what uniform electric field strength $E$ is required to balance the droplet?
items.workedSolution: Stationary balance gives $QE = mg \Rightarrow E = \frac{mg}{Q} = \frac{8.05 \times 10^{-15} \times 9.81}{9.60 \times 10^{-19}} = 8.22 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹$.

markScheme.criterion: Correct calculated value 8.22 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹.

items.stem: On a low-permittivity PTFE fixture inside an evacuated chamber, on a straight vacuum baseline of total length 3 x between +9Q on the left and +5Q on the right, point P lies 2 x from the left source. Using Coulomb constant k, what is the resultant electric field at P expressed in terms of kQ/x²?
items.workedSolution: At P, +9Q produces (9/2²) kQ/x² = 2.25 kQ/x² to the right, while +5Q at distance 1 x produces (5/1²) kQ/x² = 5.00 kQ/x² to the left. Net field = 2.75 kQ/x² to the left (C).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts (9/2²) and (5/1²) to obtain 2.75 kQ/x² to the left (C).

items.stem: Along a horizontal ceramic support rod in free space, a point charge q₁ = 2 × 10⁻⁹ C sits at x = 0 and an unknown point charge q₂ sits at x = 1 m. An axial field scan locates a zero-field null point between them at x = 0.2 m. What is the magnitude ratio |q₂ / q₁|?
items.workedSolution: At x₀ = 0.2 m, the distance from q₂ is d − x₀ = 0.8 m. Setting |q₁|/x₀² = |q₂|/(d − x₀)² gives |q₂/q₁| = (0.8/0.2)² = 16.0 (D).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ((d − x₀)/x₀)² = (0.8/0.2)² = 16.0 (D).

items.stem: Between two planar molybdenum grids of an ion-thruster prototype, an initially stationary deuteron (m = 3.34 × 10⁻²⁷ kg, q = +1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) accelerates across a uniform electric field between parallel plates 0.05 m apart with potential difference 800 V. Neglecting gravity, what speed does the deuteron reach upon arriving at the 0 V plate?
items.workedSolution: By conservation of energy, ½mv² = qV, so v = √(2qV / m) = √(2 × 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ × 800 / 3.34 × 10⁻²⁷) = 2.77 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ (B).

markScheme.criterion: Equates ½mv² = qV to obtain v = 2.77 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Inside a cryogenic linear Paul-trap alignment fixture, two like-sign point charges of −6 nC and −3 nC are fixed 0.6 m apart, with −6 nC on the left. Point P lies on the connecting axis 0.2 m from the left charge. Adopt the free-space constant k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the resultant electric field at point P?
items.workedSolution: Between like-sign charges, the individual fields at P oppose each other: |E₁| = k|q₁|/(0.2)² = 1.35 × 10³ N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/(0.4)² = 169 N C⁻¹. Subtracting gives |E_net| = 1.18 × 10³ N C⁻¹ directed to the left (B).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field contributions to obtain 1.18 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left (B).

items.stem: Inside an electrostatic aerosol-charging test section, fixed charges +2 nC at x = 0 and −8 nC at x = 0.5 m establish a zero-potential point P on the axis at x = 0.1 m. Use 1/(4πε₀) = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² with the reference of zero potential at infinite separation. Although the electric potential at P is zero, what is the resultant electric field at P?
items.workedSolution: Even though V = kq₁/r₁ + kq₂/r₂ = 0 at P, the potential gradient dV/dx is non-zero because both opposite charges drive a positive test charge to the right: E = 1.80 × 10³ N C⁻¹ + 449 N C⁻¹ = 2.25 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (B).

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes E != 0 when V = 0 and sums collinear contributions to obtain 2.25 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (B).

items.stem: Within a medical linear-accelerator pre-injector gap, a uniform electrostatic gap of width 0.045 m operates with 360 V across its parallel plates while a carrier (q = +5 × 10⁻⁸ C, m = 2 × 10⁻⁶ kg) traverses from the high-potential plate to the 0 V plate. How much electrical work is done by the electric field on the particle as it crosses from the 360 V plate to the 0 V plate?
items.workedSolution: Electrical work done across the full potential difference is W = qΔV = (5 × 10⁻⁸)(360) = 1.80 × 10⁻⁵ J (C).

items.stem: Across the central region of a wide guard-ring capacitor, three vertical equipotential lines are drawn at 240 V (left), 140 V (middle), and 40 V (right), with adjacent lines spaced 0.05 m apart. A charged dielectric bead of mass 2 × 10⁻⁵ kg and charge +4 × 10⁻⁸ C starts from rest on the middle 140 V line and moves frictionlessly horizontally to the 40 V line. What is the magnitude and direction of the uniform electric field?
items.workedSolution: Electric field points toward decreasing potential (to the right) with magnitude E = |ΔV|/s = (140 − 40) / 0.05 = 2.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹ to the right (B).

markScheme.criterion: Uses E = −ΔV/Δx to obtain 2.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹ to the right (B).

items.stem: Along the optical axis of a benchtop ion-trap demonstration rig, two stationary charges of −8 nC on the left and −5 nC on the right have separation 0.7 m, with point P marked 0.3 m from the left source. With zero potential set at infinity in vacuum, use k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the electric potential at point P?
items.workedSolution: Electric potential is a signed scalar: V = k(q₁/r₁ + q₂/r₂) with r₁ = 0.3 m and r₂ = 0.4 m. Thus V = −240 V + (−112 V) = −352 V (D).

markScheme.criterion: Sums signed scalar potentials kq₁/0.3 + kq₂/0.4 = −352 V (D).

items.stem: An uncharged capacitor is connected through a series resistor R to an ideal constant-emf battery of voltage V until fully charged to charge Q. What happens to the energy transferred by the battery?
items.workedSolution: The battery supplies energy Q V while the capacitor stores half Q V so exactly fifty percent is dissipated as thermal energy in circuit resistance regardless of resistance value. Therefore the correct statement is: The battery supplies energy Q V while the capacitor stores half Q V so exactly fifty percent is dissipated as thermal energy in circuit resistance regardless of resistance value

markScheme.criterion: Selects correct conceptual explanation: battery supplies energy Q V while the capacitor stores half Q V so exactly fifty percent is dissipated as thermal energy in circuit resistance regardless of resistance value.

options.label: A
options.text: The battery supplies energy half Q V which is stored with one hundred percent efficiency when resistance is small.
options.distractorRationale: Battery work is W = QV, not ½QV, and 50% is always dissipated regardless of R.

options.label: B
options.text: The fraction dissipated as thermal energy rises toward one hundred percent as the series resistor R is made larger.
options.distractorRationale: Larger R slows charging (longer τ = RC) but total energy lost ∫I²R dt remains ½QV.

options.label: C
options.text: The battery supplies energy Q V while the capacitor stores half Q V so exactly fifty percent is dissipated as thermal energy in circuit resistance regardless of resistance value

options.label: D
options.text: The capacitor stores the full Q V supplied by the battery while circuit resistance stores zero energy.
options.distractorRationale: Area under the linear Q–V graph is only half the rectangle QV.

items.stem: Along the reference baseline of an electrostatic beam-steering rig, charges −9 nC and +4 nC are separated horizontally by 0.5 m, with −9 nC on the left. Observation point P is situated between them, 0.3 m from the left-hand source. Model the region as vacuum with Coulomb constant k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². Find the resultant electric field vector acting at point P.
items.workedSolution: At P, both opposite-sign sources drive a positive test charge to the left. |E₁| = k|q₁|/r₁² = 899 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/r₂² = 899 N C⁻¹ (with r₂ = 0.2 m). Summing the two same-sense vectors gives E = 1.80 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left (B).

markScheme.criterion: Adds same-direction inverse-square contributions to obtain 1.80 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left (B).

options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the two individual field magnitudes instead of adding collinear vectors that point in the same direction between opposite charges.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes the correct superposition magnitude but reverses the electric field direction (forgetting field direction is defined on a positive test charge).

options.label: D

items.stem: Within an evacuated spacecraft charge-control test cell, point sources −10 nC at x = 0 and +6 nC at x = 0.8 m remain fixed while a small probe of charge −3 nC is placed at x = 0.3 m (point P). Adopt k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and zero electrostatic potential at infinite distance. What is the electric potential at P due to the two fixed source charges?
items.workedSolution: Electric potential at P depends only on the source charges: V = k(q₁/0.3 + q₂/0.5) = −300 V + (108 V) = −192 V (A).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates V = k(q₁/0.3 + q₂/0.5) = −192 V (A), independent of q_test.

options.distractorRationale: Combines the two source potentials without respecting their algebraic signs.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies the electric potential at P by the probe charge magnitude (confusing potential V with potential energy qV).

options.label: D

items.stem: Within a laboratory quadrupole pre-alignment vacuum housing, charges +4 nC and +6 nC are mounted 0.5 m apart along a horizontal line, with +4 nC on the left. An axial sensor at exterior point P sits 0.8 m to the right of +4 nC. Take the Coulomb constant as k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the resultant electric field at exterior point P?
items.workedSolution: Exterior point P is r₁ = 0.8 m to the right of +4 nC and r₂ = 0.8 − 0.5 = 0.3 m to the right of +6 nC. Superposing E_x = kq₁/r₁² + kq₂/r₂² gives 656 N C⁻¹ to the right (A).

markScheme.criterion: Uses r₁ = 0.8 m and r₂ = 0.3 m to obtain 656 N C⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: Along the reference baseline of an electrostatic beam-steering rig, isolated point charges +3 nC at x = 0 and +12 nC at x = 0.6 m are mounted along a straight insulating track. Determine the distance x from the left-hand +3 nC source to the zero-field null point between the charges.
items.workedSolution: Equating opposing field magnitudes gives q₁/x² = q₂/(0.6 − x)², so (0.6 − x)/x = √(12/3). Solving yields x = 0.6 × √3/(√3 + √12) = 0.200 m (D).

markScheme.criterion: Equates kq₁/x² = kq₂/(0.6 − x)² to obtain x = 0.200 m (D).

items.stem: Across the measurement track of a non-contact Kelvin probe bench, two fixed source charges of +4 nC (left) and −6 nC (right) are separated by 0.4 m. Point P lies on the line joining them, 0.15 m from the left source. A small probe charge of −3.2 nC is placed at P without disturbing the fixed sources. Assume vacuum permittivity such that k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the resultant electrostatic force acting on the −3.2 nC probe charge?
items.workedSolution: At P (r₁ = 0.15 m, r₂ = 0.25 m), the resultant electric field is E = 2.46 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right. Multiplying by q_test = −3.2 nC gives F = q_test E = 7.88 × 10⁻⁶ N to the left (D).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates E = 2.46 × 10³ N C⁻¹ and F = qE = 7.88 × 10⁻⁶ N to the left (D).

items.stem: In a microfluidic electrophoresis test cell (modelled in vacuum), three planar equipotentials are established labelled from left to right as 250 V, 150 V, and 50 V with uniform spacing 0.025 m between neighbouring surfaces. A test charge of +6 × 10⁻⁹ C is displaced from the leftmost surface (250 V) to the rightmost surface (50 V). What is the signed change in electrostatic potential energy ΔE_p of the charge?
items.workedSolution: Change in electric potential energy is ΔE_p = q(V_final − V_initial) = (+6 × 10⁻⁹ C)(50 − (250)) = −1.20 × 10⁻⁶ J (B).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE_p = q(V_f − V_i) = −1.20 × 10⁻⁶ J (B).

items.stem: In a head-on Rutherford backscattering experiment, a stationary nickel target nucleus (charge +28e) repels an incoming triply charged lithium nucleus (charge +3e) that momentarily comes to rest at separation 3.5 × 10⁻¹⁴ m. Take k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻², e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, and zero electric potential at infinity. What is the electrostatic potential energy of the system at closest approach, expressed in electronvolts (eV)?
items.workedSolution: At r_min, V = kZe / r_min = 1.15 × 10⁶ V. For a +3e projectile, E_p = 3eV = 3.45 × 10⁶ eV (D).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates V = 1.15 × 10⁶ V and E_p = 3V (in eV) = 3.45 × 10⁶ eV (D).

items.stem: Across the test region of a high-impedance electrometer bench, along a 0.5 m baseline, isolated charges +9 nC and +1 nC are fixed at the left and right ends respectively. Assume vacuum (k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²) and reference all scalar potentials to zero at infinity. What is the electric potential at the unique point on the line between the charges where the resultant electric field is zero?
items.workedSolution: Zero field occurs at x = 0.5 × √9/(√9 + √1) = 0.375 m from +9 nC (and 0.125 m from +1 nC). Scalar potentials add: V = k(q₁/x + q₂/(d − x)) = 288 V (D).

markScheme.criterion: Finds x = 0.375 m and sums positive scalar potentials to obtain 288 V (D).

items.stem: In a Millikan oil-drop experiment with the electric field switched off, an oil droplet of density 880 kg m⁻³ falls at a steady terminal speed of 1.10 × 10⁻⁴ m s⁻¹ through air of viscosity 1.81 × 10⁻⁵ Pa s. Neglecting air upthrust and taking $g = 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$, what is the radius of the droplet?
items.workedSolution: Equating Stokes drag and weight: $6\pi\eta r v = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \rho g \Rightarrow r = \sqrt{\frac{9\eta v}{2\rho g}} = \sqrt{\frac{9 \times 1.81 \times 10^{-5} \times 1.10 \times 10^{-4}}{2 \times 880 \times 9.81}} = 1.02 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m} = 1.02 μm$.

markScheme.criterion: Correct calculated value 1.02 μm.

items.stem: Inside an ultra-high-vacuum electrostatic calibration chamber, two isolated positive sources of charge +5Q and +4Q have separation 3 x, with +5Q at the left end. Observation point P is positioned between them at distance 2 x from +5Q. Using Coulomb constant k, what is the resultant electric field at P expressed in terms of kQ/x²?
items.workedSolution: At P, +5Q produces (5/2²) kQ/x² = 1.25 kQ/x² to the right, while +4Q at distance 1 x produces (4/1²) kQ/x² = 4.00 kQ/x² to the left. Net field = 2.75 kQ/x² to the left (A).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts (5/2²) and (4/1²) to obtain 2.75 kQ/x² to the left (A).

options.distractorRationale: Evaluates the correct inverse-square difference coefficient but reverses the resultant field direction.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds the two field magnitudes between two positive charges instead of subtracting opposing vectors.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides by unsquared distance ratios instead of squaring the distances from each charge.

items.stem: Within a dust-plasma levitation chamber evacuated to low pressure, fixed sources q₁ (left, 4 × 10⁻⁹ C) and q₂ (right) lie 0.6 m apart. The electric field vanishes at an interior point 0.2 m to the right of q₁. What is the signed charge q₂?
items.workedSolution: An interior null point requires q₁ and q₂ to have the same sign (+). Equating kq₁/x₀² = kq₂/(d − x₀)² with d − x₀ = 0.4 m gives q₂ = q₁((0.4)/(0.2))² = 4.00 × 4 × 10⁻⁹ C = +1.60 × 10⁻⁸ C (A).

markScheme.criterion: Uses q₂ = q₁((d − x₀)/x₀)² with positive sign to obtain +1.60 × 10⁻⁸ C (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Assigns the opposite sign to q₂, whereas opposite-sign charges never produce a zero-field point between them.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Scales q₁ by the unsquared distance ratio (d − x₀)/x₀ instead of ((d − x₀)/x₀)².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the squared distance ratio x₀²/(d − x₀)² instead of (d − x₀)²/x₀².
